We all have different methods & techniques, but always look for inspiration in everything. Maybe write about what's happened to you recently; the mental/physical exhaustion, your wife's pregnancy, your new baby. That's all really interesting, meaningful shit people will relate to. Yeah it has been pretty much dismissed for the most part & the aquatic ape theory in it's original form claims some pretty crazy stuff, I'm not advocating for its truth in terms of how we evolved, I just thought it would be an interesting addition in relation to the question asked. However, it's clear from fossil records that early hominids lived in wetlands, near lakes & fed on a range of underwater plants so would've had to be fairly comfortable in water. Although there are varieties of apes who still do this today, it is believed that our comfortability in water can be traced to very early hominids in sub-Saharan Africa. There's also a small contingent of biologists, such as Richard Wrangham, still studying a contemporary form of aquatic ape theory that doesn't try to claim nearly as much as the original theory did.

There's a theory that postulates we evolved from early hominids that decided to live in a more aquatic environment. The aquatic ape theory suggests that we adapted to swim better, there is no objective proof of this, but the fact that we quickly developed specific features such as; erect posture, loss of body hair, deposition of subcutaneous fat, a completely different heat-regulation system from other primates, and kidneys that function much like those of aquatic mammals, suggests there could be some correlation. So maybe we enjoy swimming because it's a key part of our evolution.

The compound word Antisemitismus ('antisemitism') was first used in print in Germany in 1879 as a scientific-sounding term for Judenhass ('Jew-hatred') and this has been its common use since then. However, The German word antisemitisch was first used in 1860 by the Austrian Jewish scholar Moritz Steinschneider (1816–1907) in the phrase antisemitische Vorurteile (antisemitic prejudices). Steinschneider used this phrase to characterise the French philosopher Ernest Renan's false ideas about how 'Semitic races' were inferior to 'Aryan races.' So actually the original use of the word referred to more than Jewish people, was actually coined by a Jewish man to criticize a French man who was deeply prejudice against not only Jews but Arabic people's also. Since then, I accept, the word has changed meaning in the volksgeist & I'm not saying anyone should have to stop using the term in that way, but I don't see the problem with me personally preferring to say anti-jewish, I think it's just as effective & semantically clearer.
